correctness.rationale: For each N>=4 and 1<=k<=N-1, with nonzero uniform hopping J and a single loss site, no-jump contraction projects asymptotically to the maximal H-invariant ker(n0). In the hard-core sector the off-site transfer is the Boolean down-map D_k. The entrywise Boolean-lattice commutator gives its full rank min(C(N-1,k),C(N-1,k-1)); A=U D-kI makes ker(D) invariant, so d_dark=max(C(N-1,k)-C(N-1,k-1),0). In the fermionic exterior-power model H=J(N n_u-k), low-energy intersection with wedge^k|0>^perp has dimension C(N-2,k), while the high-energy block has no such vector. Therefore the first-jump probabilities are min(2k/N,1) and 1-(N-k)(N-k-1)/(N(N-1)), respectively. The k=1 and k=N-1 boundaries follow; positivity of their difference only for 2<=k<=N-2. Independent exact/numeric Hamiltonian spectral intersection tests covered 36 cases; finite tests are not the proof.
residual_risks: Numerical enumeration is bounded; universal result relies on supplied proof reconstructed above.
